sections.title: Mission · Manipulate the Filesystem
paragraphs: Now that you can navigate the filesystem, learn to create, copy, move, rename, and delete files; create and remove directories; understand case sensitivity; and use simple globbing.

sections.title: touch
paragraphs: touch creates an empty file when the named file does not already exist. It can also update timestamps on existing files, but the basic recognition cue is new empty file.

sections.title: cp
paragraphs: cp means copy. cp notes.txt backup.txt duplicates the file, leaving the original in place.

sections.title: mv
paragraphs: mv means move, but it also renames files. mv notes.txt Documents/ relocates the file; mv old.txt new.txt renames it.

sections.title: rm
paragraphs: rm removes files. Command-line deletion can be unforgiving; do not assume a graphical recycle bin will recover the file.

sections.title: mkdir
paragraphs: mkdir means make directory. mkdir projects creates a directory named projects.

sections.title: rmdir
paragraphs: rmdir removes an empty directory. A simple rmdir normally will not remove a directory that still contains files.

sections.title: Exam Trap — rm vs. rmdir
sections.callout: DO NOT TREAT THEM AS INTERCHANGEABLE

sections.title: Case Sensitivity
paragraphs: Linux filenames are generally case-sensitive. notes.txt, Notes.txt, and NOTES.txt can be three different files. Report.txt and report.txt may not refer to the same file.
sections.callout: GSA.txt IS NOT gsa.txt · CAPITALIZATION MATTERS

sections.title: Simple Globbing
paragraphs: Globbing lets the shell match groups of filenames using wildcard patterns rather than requiring every filename individually. Two important wildcards are * and ?.

sections.title: The * Wildcard
paragraphs: * matches zero or more characters. *.txt can match notes.txt, report.txt, and gsa.txt. gsa* can match names beginning with gsa.

sections.title: The ? Wildcard
paragraphs: ? matches exactly one character. file?.txt can match file1.txt or fileA.txt, but not file10.txt because 10 contains two characters.

sections.title: Globbing with Commands
paragraphs: Wildcard patterns can be supplied to ordinary commands. cp *.txt backup/ copies matching text files. rm *.tmp removes matching temporary files. A wildcard can make a command operate on many files at once.
sections.callout: THE SHELL EXPANDS THE PATTERN BEFORE THE COMMAND ACTS

sections.title: GSA Safety Lesson
paragraphs: Before using a destructive command with a wildcard, understand what the pattern matches. rm * can target many entries. The shell follows the command given; precision matters.
